title: Where are the angles in spectacles and a wallet?
description: Spectacles and a wallet are looked at to find two parts that turn about one place. The two parts are drawn as rays and the point where they are joined is found. Keeko's doubt, that the vertex is the free end of the side piece, is broken by the free tip, where the two arms do not meet.
teaching_notes: One idea: in any object with a hinge, the two parts that turn are the arms and the hinge is the vertex. Watch for students who pick the free end of one part as the vertex.

source: Look at the pictures of spectacles, wallet and other common objects. Identify the angles in them by marking out their arms and vertices.
video_script.why: The child finds the two arms and the vertex of the angle in common objects that open about a hinge.
video_script.substitution: Draw each of the two parts that turn as a ray that starts at the hinge.
video_script.anchor: a pair of spectacles with a side piece opened, and a wallet opened a little
video_script.wrong_answer: the vertex is the free end of the side piece
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the vertex is the free end of the side piece, the tip behind the ear. The free tip is only where one arm ends, and the arms do not meet there, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The two parts that turn are the arms, and the vertex is the hinge

final_answer.value: In each object the two parts that turn are the arms and the hinge is the vertex. In the spectacles they are the side piece and the frame, and in the wallet they are its two halves
final_answer.spoken: in each object the two parts that turn are the arms and the hinge is the vertex. In the spectacles they are the side piece and the frame, and in the wallet they are its two halves

never_show: the hinge named as the vertex, before the answer beat
maths_rules: An angle is formed by two rays with a common starting point; the rays are the arms and the starting point is the vertex.
In spectacles the side piece and the frame turn about the hinge, so they lie along the two arms.
In a wallet the two halves turn about the place where they are joined, so they lie along the two arms.
The vertex is the one point where both arms start, so in each object it is the hinge.
Slip: the free end of the side piece is only where one arm ends, so it is not the vertex.
video_script.design: One idea: find the hinge, then the two parts that turn there. The spectacles and the wallet stay on the board and open a little. The wrong idea is that the free end of the side piece is the vertex.
open_questions: The worklist answer also lists a stapler, a hinged box and a box with an open flap. The book text names only spectacles and a wallet, so the video uses those two and keeps to the book.
